elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"
"upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor"
"Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term."

elements.element: Termination right operative notwithstanding the take-or-pay commitment (no contradictory bar)
elements.evidence: 2.1 now reads "subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4" in place of "without reduction or termination rights"
"thirty (30) days' prior written notice" — shorter than the 60–90 day fallback window

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees (cap only; condition absent if no fee)
elements.evidence: "without penalty, early-termination charge, or other liability" — no fee imposed, so cap condition is absent

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a term." — no end-of-term 90-day Vendor right is granted

offending_extra_words: without penalty, early-termination charge, or other liability
subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4
reasons: The inserted Section 9.4 satisfies every atomic element of the preferred position: a Customer convenience right, 30 days' prior written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a term.

The fallback is not satisfied as a standalone bargain (30-day notice is below the 60–90 day band and no end-of-term Vendor right exists), but that is irrelevant because the locked preferred level is fully met.

Minimality fails: the insertion carries surplus language beyond what the preferred position requires — "in whole or in part" expands scope to partial termination, and "without penalty, early-termination charge, or other liability" duplicates protection already implied by an unconditional convenience right.

The Section 2.1 edit rewrites the operative tail rather than making the narrowest change; a targeted carve-out (e.g. striking "without ... termination rights" or adding "except as set out in Section 9.4") would suffice. The broad phrase "subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement" sweeps in all termination rights, not just convenience, weakening the take-or-pay commitment more than needed.

Intent is preserved: the USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment, Section 9.3 cause-based termination triggers, and defined terms (Fees, Order Form) all remain effective, and Section 9.4 is a real cross-reference with no dangling mechanic.
